stimulus: A health clinic recorded the waiting times of patients on one morning. The table shows the grouped data. The frequency for patients waiting from 20 to 29 minutes was obscured and is represented by $x$. The estimated mean waiting time was $23.5$ minutes. The clinic manager claims that the middle 50% of waiting times lies entirely within the modal class.
stem: Use the table to answer the questions below.

params.caption: Waiting times of patients at a health clinic

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Determine the class midpoint for the waiting-time class 20-29 minutes.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: State the modal class and the median class.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Complete the statement below. Give the estimates correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.statement: The lower quartile is {} min, the upper quartile is {} min and the interquartile range is {} min. Therefore, the manager's claim is {}.

rubric.criterion: Uses the grouped-data mean with the class midpoints
rubric.template: Uses the grouped-data mean with the class midpoints
rubric.hint: Multiply each class frequency by its class midpoint, add these products, and divide by the total frequency to find the grouped-data mean.
Form the mean equation $\frac{T+mx}{N+x}=\bar{x}$ by adding the unknown class contribution to the known weighted total and total frequency.
Solve your mean equation carefully for $x$ by clearing the denominator first and collecting the $x$ terms.

rubric.criterion: Interprets the solution as a valid whole-number frequency
rubric.template: Interprets the solution as a valid whole-number frequency
rubric.hint: Check that your value of $x$ can represent a frequency by confirming that it is a non-negative whole number.

rubric.criterion: Calculates lower quartile as $9.5 + \frac{12.5-4}{9}\times10 = 18.9$ to 1 d.p., using "their" frequency
rubric.template: Calculates lower quartile as $9.5 + \frac{12.5-4}{9}\times10 = {d.lower_quartile}$ to 1 d.p., using "their" frequency
rubric.hint: Use your frequency in the lower-quartile interpolation formula $L+\frac{p-c}{f}\times w$ and round the estimate to one decimal place.

rubric.criterion: Calculates upper quartile as $19.5 + \frac{37.5-13}{28}\times10 = 28.3$ to 1 d.p., using "their" frequency
rubric.template: Calculates upper quartile as $19.5 + \frac{37.5-13}{{b.i}}\times10 = {d.upper_quartile}$ to 1 d.p., using "their" frequency
rubric.hint: Use your frequency in the upper-quartile interpolation formula $L+\frac{p-c}{f}\times w$ and round the estimate to one decimal place.
Subtract your lower-quartile estimate from your upper-quartile estimate, use $\ldots$ for any continuing decimal if needed, and round the interquartile range to one decimal place.

rubric.criterion: Concludes that the claim is false since "their" lower quartile is below the lower boundary $19.5$ of the modal class
rubric.template: Concludes that the claim is false since "their" lower quartile is below the lower boundary $19.5$ of the modal class
rubric.hint: Compare your lower-quartile estimate with the lower boundary of the modal class and use this comparison to decide whether the claim is false.

rubric.criterion: Expresses the quartile estimates and interquartile range to 1 decimal place
rubric.template: Expresses the quartile estimates and interquartile range to 1 decimal place
rubric.hint: Write both quartile estimates and the interquartile range consistently to one decimal place.

worked_solution:
(a) The midpoint of the class is $\frac{20+29}{2}=24.5$.

(b) The known total frequency is $4+9+6+3=22$. The known total of frequency multiplied by midpoint is $(4\times4.5)+(9\times14.5)+(6\times34.5)+(3\times44.5)=489$. Therefore,
\[
\frac{489+24.5x}{22+x}=23.5.
\]
Multiplying through gives $489+24.5x=517+23.5x$, so $x=28$.

(c) The largest frequency is $28$, so the modal class is 20-29 min. The total frequency is $50$, and the median position is the $25$th value. The cumulative frequency reaches $41$ in the class 20-29 min, so this is also the median class.

(d) The lower-quartile position is $\frac{50}{4}=12.5$. This lies in the class 10-19 min, giving $Q_1=9.5+\frac{12.5-4}{9}\times10=18.94\ldots$, or $18.9$ min.

The upper-quartile position is $\frac{3(50)}{4}=37.5$. This lies in the class 20-29 min, giving $Q_3=19.5+\frac{37.5-13}{28}\times10=28.25$, or $28.3$ min.

The interquartile range is $28.25-18.94\ldots=9.30\ldots$, or $9.3$ min. The claim is false because $Q_1=18.9$ min is below $19.5$ min, the lower class boundary of the modal class.

misconceptions.name: Range reported as an interval
misconceptions.remediation: The interquartile range is one number, found by subtracting the lower quartile from the upper quartile. It is not the pair of quartile values or a class interval.

misconceptions.name: Modal frequency given instead of modal class
misconceptions.remediation: The frequency 28 identifies the most common class. The modal class is the waiting-time interval 20-29 min.

misconceptions.name: Used class limits instead of class boundaries
misconceptions.remediation: For grouped-data interpolation, use class boundaries. The relevant lower boundaries are 9.5 and 19.5, not 10 and 20.
